title: XOR and XNOR Gates Explained Simply | PUC and ISC
description:
Aarav's staircase light has two switches, and either one can turn it on or off. Which logic gate thinks like this? In this animated lesson we meet the XOR (exclusive OR) gate and its partner, the XNOR gate.

On a live breadboard the truth table fills row by row as the switch tiles toggle, the lamp shows the output and an oscilloscope traces A, B and Y: XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ, XNOR gives 1 when they are the same. We build the XOR formula from basic gates, see why two-way stair switches work like XOR, and learn two tricks (a switchable NOT and the odd-or-even check). A worked example proves a three-gate circuit is XOR, followed by the exam trap (XOR is not OR in the last row), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 55 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 8: Introduction to Digital Electronics. Boards: Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 8 Introduction to Digital Electronics | ISC Class 12 Computer Science: elementary logic gates including XOR and XNOR. Logic gates are no longer in the rationalised NCERT/CBSE Physics book.
